classification_signals: Abstract: 'A total of 35 commercial buildings have been selected in the survey. Two typical office blocks were further analysed based on a lighting simulation program.' (p. 1)
Section 2: 'The daylighting performance of office buildings was determined through a survey of 35 office blocks completed in different years.' (p. 2)

Section 3: 'In order to gain more ideas about the indoor daylighting performance, daylight factors (DF) inside the office spaces at low, middle and high floor levels for two buildings (Buildings 20 and 30) were simulated.' (p. 5)
Section 3.2: 'RADIANCE [20] is a computer simulation package for simulating and visualizing lighting in and around architectural environments using the backward ray-tracing technique.' (p. 5)
title: An analysis of daylighting performance for office buildings in Hong Kong

minimum_safe_summary: This empirical study investigated daylighting performance and energy implications in 35 Hong Kong office buildings, with detailed simulations of two typical blocks using RADIANCE. Key findings indicate that about one-third of perimeter office areas achieve an average daylight factor of 5%, and proper daylight-linked lighting controls could save over 25% of electric lighting energy. Daylighting performance is significantly influenced by window area, glass type, external obstructions, and room depth, with DFs rapidly decreasing away from windows and at lower floors. Glare indices were generally below discomfort thresholds. The study concludes that current building façade designs are conducive to effective daylighting, offering substantial energy savings. No explicit limitations were stated.
